finding: Graph/RV maker target capacity is mechanically coupled to same-side touch depth twice: the relation generator uses min best-bid size to cap bundle notional, and the multi-leg broker caps units at 25% of same-side touch size before enforcing minimum order size. This creates a hard queue-ahead floor and can make larger/worse queues mechanically permit larger target sizes.
interpretation: This is an execution-sizing identification defect, not alpha evidence. Same-side queue ahead should affect fill/completion probability. It should not by itself determine how much capacity the strategy is allowed to target. A successor should size from hard risk/capital limits and independently measured executable unwind depth, then apply queue-aware same-window completion and partial-fill/unwind EV before admission.
required_common_sample_experiment: Use identical chronological Graph/RV candidates and identical executable prices, verified fees, slippage and deadlines.
Arm A: incumbent relation-generator plus broker same-side-touch size coupling.
Arm B: queue-decoupled target capacity bounded by risk and independently measured cumulative executable unwind depth.
Keep queue ahead as a separate causal fill/completion input in both arms.
Measure per-leg fill states, all-leg completion, partial-fill frequency, abort/unwind loss, capital-hours and fill-conditioned net PnL at 1x, 1.5x and 2x execution cost stress.
Do not promote Arm B merely for higher fill count; require non-degrading executable EV and hard-safety compliance.
